JUDGEMENT CALLS: no wire on this sheet hops or jogs over another, and none of the sites carries a solder dot noticeably fatter than the strokes, so every intersection is read as drawn ink meeting drawn ink. All eleven critical sites are recorded explicitly:
  S1 (680,291), S2 (526,295), S3 (362,298), S4 (118,306) = JUNCTION. Each is a plain T where a column (or the V-AC's top lead) starts on the top rail and runs only downward; the rail is continuous through the crop. A crossing reading is not even expressible at a deg-3 T without stranding the column head on a 1-terminal net.
  S29 (832,687), S30 (528,693), S32 (363,695) = JUNCTION. Same plain T's on the bottom rail. At S29 the rail terminates - there is no ink east of the column - so the column must join it.
  S18 (101,500), S19 (359,503), S20 (529,502), S21 (680,502), S22 (833,504) = JUNCTION. These are the five deg-4 points where a column crosses the middle rail. All are plain X's: pixel-level there is no hop arc and no lateral jog (the tracer's hop scores of 1.9-5.7 are 2-6 degree bends of the slightly wavy hand-drawn rail, all under the 6.0 threshold, and nothing like a drawn semicircle which swings ~90 degrees). Per the dataset's ink prior a bare crossing is a junction. Consequence of the other reading, e.g. at S20: n5 would split into {D4 bottom, Z13 top} and {C8 right, Z3 bottom, L7 left, D12 top}, cutting the ladder into disconnected upper/lower halves at that column - and doing that at all five columns would break the drawing into a set of isolated series strings, with the GND symbol reaching only C8's left plate. At S18 specifically, junction is what puts the AC source's negative side and the 3A source's positive side on ground, which is the only reading in which the ground symbol grounds anything.
  Non-critical sites S5, S7, S8, S10, S11, S13, S15, S16, S17, S23, S24, S27, S31 are the handwritten value labels ('5uH', '15uF', '8V', '1kHz', '4uH', '9uF', '2k ohm', '1uH', '3A') brushing a wire or a component box; left at the default they touch no terminal (S31 is recorded as a junction anyway because it is also the real T of the x~669 column onto the bottom rail).
